title: A hidden-state shift can cause a language model to repeat one token
summary: Researchers isolated a shift shared across responses during language-model preference training. Inserting the learned shift into an untreated model reproduced a failure in which one token dominated generation. The failure appeared in 14 of 17 tested model lineages under the study’s per-token ranking objective.
ai_technology: Preference-optimized language models, including Llama-2 and Llama-3.1
organization: The University of Tokyo; TIER IV; Huawei

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, §§4–5 and 7, Appendix B.17, and primary intervention controls

evidence.tested: The authors isolated the shared offset, compared transplantation with magnitude-matched random directions, and tested masking of the component in the training loss.
evidence.unknown: The failure depends on model and objective. Related hidden shifts were also observed without generation collapse in tested standard preference-training runs.
evidence.ai_role: The researchers isolated a common direction learned during preference training and tested its contribution by transplanting it into an untreated language model.
